findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires being both admin and owner
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A team admin who is not the owner (and vice versa) therefore evaluates to false, so legitimate team admins/owners who are not also the booking organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN. The condition should be an OR, matching the variable name and the intended authorization.

findings.title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests to someone else's booking
findings.body: Authorization passes if the caller is merely an attendee (matched by email). The UI only exposes this action on the organizer's bookings page, but via the API any attendee with a Cal.com account can add unlimited arbitrary guests to the organizer's booking, triggering calendar updates and invitation emails from the organizer without organizer approval. This is a privilege escalation beyond the organizer-only feature being added.

findings.title: No booking status or timing check before adding guests
findings.body: The handler never checks booking.status or start/end time. Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-ended bookings; the handler then persists attendees, calls updateCalendarAttendees, and sendAddGuestsEmails emits ICS files with status CONFIRMED. This can resurrect/confuse dead bookings and sends misleading confirmed invites for events that will not happen. It should reject non-accepted and past bookings.

findings.title: Calendar is updated with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: credentials are loaded via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and EventManager is built from the calling user, while evt.destinationCalendar belongs to the booking organizer. When the caller is a team admin or attendee (both explicitly authorized above), the organizer's calendar event is updated using the wrong user's credentials, so the calendar update will fail or target the wrong account even though the DB attendees were already added. Credentials/EventManager should be based on booking.user (already loaded with credentials in the query).

findings.title: Server schema allows duplicate, case-variant, and unbounded guest lists
findings.body: guests is just z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness, normalization, or max length. The handler's dedupe is case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`) and does not dedupe within the input itself, and the blacklist check lowercases the blacklist but not the guest. An API caller can therefore create duplicate attendee rows (e.g. 'A@x.com' and 'a@x.com', or the same email twice, causing createMany duplicates) and submit arbitrarily large lists to spam calendar invites/emails. The client-side refine in AddGuestsDialog does not protect the API.

findings.title: Emails are classified using the raw guest list instead of the guests actually added
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is passed the raw input rather than uniqueGuests. sendAddGuestsEmails treats any attendee whose email is in that list as a new guest and sends them a full AttendeeScheduledEmail. An existing attendee who was filtered out as already-present therefore incorrectly receives a fresh scheduled invitation instead of the 'guests added' notification, and filtered/blacklisted handling diverges from what was actually persisted. Pass uniqueGuests.
